view.lede: The Downs, right-handed: one of the five generic courses that every course without its own build races on for now (undulating, downhill turn). A rolling triangle of about 1m4f on the downs: a climb along the back straight, a sweeping downhill turn into a 3½f run-in that rises again in the last furlong, and a downhill 7f straight course. Dressed as a downland course.
notes: Brighton and Lingfield (turf), and the two big downland courses until their own builds are in the game.
About 12.5f round, a 3.31f run-in. Drawn from a few numbers (the corners and bends of the loop, the chutes), so it can be reshaped quickly.
Downland course: medium and smaller pieces from the grandstand crib sheet on one front line, the crowd up to the rail; the festival in the infield opposite and up the stand side.
Choose Medium or Low under Quality in the race view's bar. Auto steps down by itself.
